newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian stocks rebound, but upside seen limited.
newsitem.headline: Austrian stocks rebound, but upside seen limited.

text.p: Austrian shares followed leading European markets on Monday to close just below the day's highs, but traders said volume remained slack and doubted the market could muster up the strength to break out of its current range.

The ATX index of 21 blue chips rose 8.53 points or 0.8 percent to close at 1,030.12, down from the day's high of 1,031. Among its constituents, 18 shares outnumbered just two decliners, one stock was unchanged.

Most market participants see the index locked in a narrow range between 1,020 and 1,040 points. "We won't get out of this very easily," one trader said, adding that today's rebound was in large parts a technical reaction to Friday's losses.
Austro-Italian insurer EA-Generali led the day's advancers, rising 80 schillings or 3.6 percent to 2,870 after the group spearheaded a last-minute bid for government sell-off candidate Creditanstalt.

A spokesman for Finance Minister Viktor Klima said the minister and his advisors, JP Morgan, were looking into the offer and that Klima may report his findings at the weekly cabinet meeting on Tuesday.
Creditanstalt's ordinary shares gained five schillings to 666, while its preferred shares added on 1.1 schilling to 479.

High-grade steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm gained 17 schillings or 2.2 percent to 776 after reporting a 12 percent gain in first-half profits. Boehler was the third most actively traded stock on turnover of over 17,000 lots.
VA Tech announces its first-half earnings on Tuesday, while VA Stahl reports on Friday.
The September ATX future gained 7.3 points to 1,029.3 on turnover of 231 contracts.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index advanced 3.08 points, or 0.8 percent, to close at at 403.24 -- Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
